threat_model.model: compromised-host (project default): attacker controls a host and may send arbitrary packets, but cannot reconfigure the control plane
threat_model.reason: Fixture. The point of the test is that the threshold is CONTROL-PLANE supplied and therefore NOT attacker-chosen, which is what makes pinning it sound.

assume.ref: cp_action_param_keyless_tna fixture: the deployed controller installs set_threshold as the default entry
assume.reason: The table is keyless, so set_threshold is reachable ONLY as the default action. p4c defaults it to NoAction, which leaves the threshold at 0 and makes every emitted case a single-send false positive. This clause is also the one that must reach TNA: it used to be honoured by the bmv2 table stepper alone.

assume.ref: cp_action_param_keyless_tna fixture: the deployed controller installs threshold = 20
assume.reason: Without this the synthesized action argument is free-symbolic, so the solver picks 0 and the sink flips on the first packet. On a keyless table the argument is minted by setTableDefaultEntries rather than by evalTableControlEntries, which is the pin path this fixture covers.
